about: Hunahpu and Xbalanque clear their field a second time and decide to watch it by night. They tell their grandmother and their mother that someone is making fools of them, arm themselves, and hide among the felled trees. At midnight all the animals, small and great, gather and come crying “Rise up, trees! Rise up, vines!” The puma and the jaguar get away; the twins catch the deer and the rabbit only by the tails, which snap off, and that is why their tails are short; the fox, the coyote, the peccary and the coati get away too. Last comes the rat. They catch it in a cloth, squeeze its head and burn its tail over the fire, which is why the rat's tail is bare and its eyes bulge. The rat begs for its life and its food, and tells them that field work is not their calling: the ball gear of their fathers, Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu, who died in Xibalba, the rings, the hand-guards and the rubber ball, hangs up under the roof of the house, hidden by their grandmother. They promise it maize, chile, beans, pek and cacao, and whatever is left over. At noon they carry the rat in hidden and set it up at a corner of the house, ask their grandmother for chile sauce, spill the water jar and send her to the river for more. In the sauce they see the rat climbing to the ball. They send a gnat-like creature, the xan, to pierce the grandmother's jar, so that she cannot stop it; they send their mother after her; the rat cuts the gear down, and the twins hide it on the road to the ball court. Then they go to the river, stop the jar, and walk home ahead of their grandmother. So the ball came to them.

sentences.t: Cate chicut xqui tiquiba chic abixic.
sentences.l: Then again-then they-began again field-work.
sentences.i: Then once again they set about the work of the field.
sentences.n: A new paragraph begins here (ours; Ximénez does not indent). Cate chicut 'then once more': cate 'then' + chicut, chic 'again' + cut 'then' written as one word. The t of Cate may be doubled in the MS (catte); it is printed Cate, as everywhere else. xqui tiquiba 'they began': x- + qui- 'they' + tiquiba, the verb of planting used for beginning (as in earlier parts). abixic 'field work', abix 'maize field' + -ic. The field the animals undid in the last part is cleared a second time.

sentences.t: Xa vi xuban chi rib vleuh ruꜭ catoh che;
sentences.l: Just (vi) it-did-it to itself earth with cutting tree;
sentences.i: Just as before, it was done of itself (?): the earth, with the felling of the trees;
sentences.n: xuban 'it did it': x- + v- 'it' (singular) + ban 'do'. chi rib 'to itself, of itself': rib, r- + ib 'self'. In the last part the hoe and the axe worked by themselves (chutuquel), and the sentence is taken as saying the same again (inferred); Brasseur reads it as the twins' work ('ils en firent de même à la surface du sol avec les arbres coupés'). ruꜭ 'with': the g-shaped letter carries a small comma below here, read as the cuatrillo, not tz', with Brasseur's ruq. catoh che 'the cutting of trees': catoh has plain c (Brasseur gatoh); it is the q'atoj of the last part, the word certain, and the toggle restores the q'.

sentences.t: ta xcam chicu qui naoh chiri pa catoh che, pa cupuh puch: “Xa ca varah ri cabix. Ana vi chi na ca bano vlo, la quita chi ca rileo,” xeꜭha cut.
sentences.l: then they-took again-then their-thought there in cutting tree, in clearing(?) also: “Only we-watch(?) the our-field. Perhaps(?) (vi) (chi) still the-one-doing-it(?) hither, (la) (quita) (chi) we-catch(?),” they-said then.
sentences.i: and they took counsel there once more, among the felled trees and the cleared ground (?): “We will only keep watch over our field. Perhaps (?) whoever is doing this will come here again, and we may catch them (?),” they said.
sentences.n: xcam qui naoh 'they took counsel', word for word 'took their thought', the phrase of 006: cam 'take' (toggle k'am, Brasseur x-qam; the 'take' verb is still an open question). The plain c of xcam is the establishment's reading (Brasseur qam). cupuh 'clearing' as in the last part (inferred). Xa ca varah 'we will only watch': ca 'we' + varah, not otherwise known; 'keep watch' follows Brasseur ('nous veillerons') and may be var 'sleep' made a verb, 'keep the night' (inferred; toggle by the letters). ri cabix 'our field': in the twins' mouth c- is ca- 'our' before a vowel (toggle qab'ix). The second sentence is hard. Ana vi is not otherwise known ('perhaps' after Brasseur's 'Peut-être', a guess); ca bano vlo is taken as 'the one who does it, (coming) hither' (inferred). la quita is not explained. chi ca rileo is a doubtful reading: the letters look like rileo or rieo, with no descender for q, where Brasseur prints chi ka riqo (riq 'find'); his French is 'parviendrons-nous à surprendre', and 'catch' follows that sense and is a guess.

sentences.t: Ta xcam qui naoh.
sentences.l: Then they-took their-thought.
sentences.i: So they made up their minds.
sentences.n: Ta xcam qui naoh, the same words as at the start of the sentence before, here closing the plan: they had taken their counsel (toggle xk'am, as above).

sentences.t: Xe opon chicut chi ha: “Naqui ri lo, coh michouic, ix catit! Nima quim chic, nima quechelah chi puch ri cabix ta xoh opon mier, ix catit,” xeꜭha cut chire catit, chire pu qui chuch.
sentences.l: They-arrived-there again-then at house: “What the perhaps, we-are-being-tricked(?), you our-grandmother! Great grass now, great forest (chi) also the our-field when we-arrived just-now, you our-grandmother,” they-said then to-her their-grandmother, to-her also their mother.
sentences.i: Then they came home again: “What can this be? Someone is making fools of us (?), grandmother! There is tall grass again, and a great forest too over our field (?), when we went there just now, grandmother,” they said to their grandmother, and to their mother.
sentences.n: chi ha 'at the house', home (ha 'house', toggle ja; ha 'water' is ja'). Naqui ri lo 'what can this be': naqui 'what' + ri + lo 'perhaps'. The letter after qui is r, as in chiri on the same page; Brasseur prints Naki vilo. coh michouic 'we are being made fools of': coh, c- + oh 'we', + michouic, the -ou- form of the last part's Apachinac coh michouic 'who is tricking us', where oh is the one tricked and the doer is named in front; here no doer is named (a guess, after Brasseur 'nous avons été joués'). ix catit 'you, grandmother' is spoken to her (toggle qatit); in the narrative chire catit is 'to their grandmother' (toggle katit), as in 014 and 015. quim 'grass' and quechelah 'forest' are known words (toggle k'im, k'echelaj). chi puch: chi is not clear here, taken as chi 'at' before ri cabix (toggle by the letters). mier 'just now', a word modern K'iche' still uses (Brasseur 'tout-à-l'heure'). chire catit, chire pu qui chuch 'to their grandmother, and to their mother', the couplet of the household.

sentences.t: “Xcoh be cut, xchi ca varah, rumal mavi vꜩ ca ban chique,” xeꜭha.
sentences.l: “We-shall go then, shall we-watch(?), because not good is-done to-us,” they-said.
sentences.i: “We will go back, then, and keep watch, for what is being done to us is not good,” they said.
sentences.n: Xcoh be 'we shall go': x(c)- 'shall' + oh 'we' + be 'go'. xchi ca varah 'we shall keep watch' (varah as above, inferred). ca ban 'it is done': c- (ongoing) + ban, with no person prefix, so passive in sense. chique 'to us': in the twins' speech qu- is 'us' (toggle chiqe, as in earlier parts), not chique 'to them'.

sentences.t: Catecut xe baꜩonic.
sentences.l: Then-then they-armed(?).
sentences.i: Then they armed themselves (?).
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). xe baꜩonic: xe 'they' + baꜩon + -ic, not otherwise known; 'armed themselves' follows Brasseur ('ils s'armèrent') and is a guess. The tz ligature is plain (toggle tz).

sentences.t: Catecut qui bic chic pa qui catoh che; chiri cut xe maꜩehe vi, e mucumuxinac chic chiri.
sentences.l: Then-then their-going again to their cutting tree; there then they-hid(?) (vi), they hidden(?) now there.
sentences.i: Then off they went again to their felled trees, and there they hid themselves, lying in hiding (?) there.
sentences.n: qui bic 'their going' is a doubtful reading: the word ends ic (Brasseur prints bie, OCR for be); taken as be 'go' + -ic (toggle b'ik). qui catoh che 'their felled trees', catoh as in ¶1 (toggle q'atoj). xe maꜩehe vi 'they hid there' follows Brasseur ('s'y cachèrent'; inferred), with vi pointing to the place. e mucumuxinac 'they lying hidden': mucumux, perhaps from muk 'bury, cover' doubled, + -inac, the ending of a state reached (inferred; Brasseur 'abrités … dans l'ombre').

sentences.t: Ta xe cuchu cu quib ronohel chicop; xa hun xqui zep vi quib ronohel chuti chicop, nima chicop.
sentences.l: Then they-gathered(?) then themselves all animal; only one they-joined(?) (vi) themselves all small animal, great animal.
sentences.i: Then all the animals gathered themselves together; as one they joined themselves (?), all the small animals and the great animals.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). xe cuchu cu quib 'they gathered themselves': cuchu, read as the verb of gathering (inferred, after Brasseur 'se rassemblèrent'), with quib 'themselves' (qui- + ib). With a reflexive the prefix would be xqui-, as in the next clause; here xe is written (MS xecuchu). xa hun xqui zep vi quib 'as one they joined themselves': zep is not otherwise known (Brasseur 'chaque espèce s'unissant'; a guess; toggle sep). chuti chicop, nima chicop 'small animals, great animals', the pair for all the animals of the last part.

sentences.t: Are puch tiꜭil vꜭux acab ta xe petic, xe chauiheic conohel.
sentences.l: This also planted its-heart night when they-came, they-spoke(?) all-of-them.
sentences.i: And it was at the very heart of the night that they came, all of them speaking (?).
sentences.n: tiꜭil vꜭux acab 'midnight', word for word 'the planted (fixed) heart of the night': tiꜭil, from tik 'plant', is the tiquil of earlier parts, here written with the g-shaped letter, read ꜭ with Brasseur's tiqil (toggle by the letter, tik'il). acab 'night' has plain c (house aꜫab; toggle aq'ab', as in 015). The words ta xe petic, xe chauiheic conohel are on the image but missing from Brasseur, who prints only ta x-e petic, are qui chabal ri. xe chauiheic is a doubtful reading, read letter by letter; the word and its division are unclear, perhaps a form of chau 'speak' (a guess; toggle by the letters).

sentences.t: Ta xe petic, are qui ꜭhabal ri: “Iaclin che, iaclin caam,” xeꜭha ta xe petic.
sentences.l: When they-came, this their-speech the: “Rise tree, rise vine,” they-said when they-came.
sentences.i: As they came, this was what they said: “Rise up, trees! Rise up, vines!” So they said as they came.
sentences.n: qui ꜭhabal 'their speech': ꜭha 'speak' + -bal (MS gh, read ꜭh). Iaclin 'rise up!' is taken from yac 'lift, raise' (Brasseur 'levez-vous'); the -lin is not otherwise known, and Brasseur notes that the form does not fit K'iche' grammar (inferred; toggle yaklin). che, caam 'trees, vines', the pair for the whole forest (caam toggle k'a'm). ta xe petic 'as they came' frames the speech on both sides.

sentences.t: Que nebebic xe che, xe caam, ta xe yopihic, ta xe cutun cu chi qui vach.
sentences.l: They thronging(?) under tree, under vine, when they-approached(?), when they-appeared then at their face.
sentences.i: They came thronging (?) under the trees, under the vines; they drew near, and showed themselves before the twins' eyes.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). Que nebebic 'they thronging' is not otherwise known (Brasseur 'leurs multitudes se pressant'; a guess). xe che, xe caam 'under the trees, under the vines': xe 'root, foot, beneath' (toggle xe'), a couplet. xe yopihic 'they drew near' (Brasseur 's'approchérent'; inferred), the verb of ¶6's xyopih. xe cutun 'they appeared': cutun 'be shown' (toggle k'utun). chi qui vach 'before their faces', the twins'.

sentences.t: Are cut v nabe ri coh, balam; xrah cu qui chapo, mavi xu ya rib.
sentences.l: This then its-first the puma, jaguar; wanted then they-catch-them, not it-gave itself.
sentences.i: The first were the puma and the jaguar; the twins tried to catch them, but they would not give themselves up.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). v nabe 'the first'. coh, balam 'puma, jaguar', the first pair of the animal list in the last part (coh 'puma' with plain c, as 015; toggle koj; Brasseur 'le Lion, le Tigre'). xrah … qui chapo 'they wanted … to catch them': xrah 'wanted' (x- + r- + ah) and the wanted action after it, as in earlier parts. mavi xu ya rib 'it did not give itself up': ya 'give' with rib 'itself', singular for the pair.

sentences.t: Ta xyopih chic queh, vmul; xa cuchu he xqui chap vi, xa cu xcupu cab, canahoc vhe queh pa qui cab.
sentences.l: Then approached(?) again deer, rabbit; only gathered(?) tail they-caught (vi), only then broke-off(?) hand, remained its-tail deer in their hand.
sentences.i: Then the deer and the rabbit came near; it was only their tails, bunched together (?), that the twins caught hold of, and these just snapped off (?) in their hands: the deer's tail was left in their hands.
sentences.n: queh, vmul 'deer, rabbit' (toggle kej, umul, as 015). xa cuchu he is a doubtful division (MS xacuchuhe; Brasseur xa cuch u he): cuchu 'gathered' as in ¶4 and he 'tail' (vhe 'its tail', toggle je', uje'), after Brasseur 'les queues rapprochées l'une de l'autre' (a guess). xcupu cab: the image has cab where Brasseur prints cub; cupu, perhaps the cupuh 'pull up' of ¶1, is taken as 'came away, snapped' (inferred), and cab 'hand' has plain c, as pa qui cab 'in their hands' after it (toggle q'ab', as in 015). canahoc 'remained': canah 'remain' + -oc (toggle kanajoq).

sentences.t: Ta xu cam ri vhe queh ruꜭ vhe vmul, ri xzcatac qui he.
sentences.l: Then it-took the its-tail deer with its-tail rabbit, the became-short(?) their tail.
sentences.i: So the deer came by its tail, and the rabbit by its tail (?): their tails became short (?).
sentences.n: xu cam 'it took' (toggle k'am, the 'take' verb as ¶1): x- + u- 'it', singular. The twins' own verbs take qui- (xqui chap, xqui poroh), so the sentence is read like ¶8's xu cam ri vhe cho, 'the rat took on its tail': the deer, with the rabbit, came by the tail it has (inferred). Brasseur makes the twins the doers ('ayant pris ainsi la queue du Cerf et celle du Lapin'). ri xzcatac qui he 'their tails became short': xzcatac is not otherwise known, and 'short' follows Brasseur ('une queue tout-à-fait courte'; a guess; toggle by the letters). This is why the deer and the rabbit have short tails.

sentences.t: Ma cu xqui ya quib ri yac, vtiu, aꜫ, ziz; xe icouic conohel chicop chi qui vach ri Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.l: Not then they-gave themselves the fox(?), coyote, peccary, coati(?); they-passed all-of-them animal at their face the Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.i: Nor did the fox (?), the coyote, the peccary and the coati (?) give themselves up; all the animals went past before the eyes of Hunahpu and Xbalanque.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). The rest of the list of the last part: yac 'fox' (here the letter is y, where 015 printed iac; Brasseur Yac, 'le Renard'; inferred, toggle yak), vtiu 'coyote' (toggle utiw), aꜫ 'peccary', with the tresillo (Brasseur ak, 'le Sanglier'; toggle aq'), ziz 'coati' (Brasseur 'le Porc-Epic'; inferred, toggle sis). xe icouic 'they passed by' (toggle ik'owik, as in earlier parts).

sentences.t: Chi catat chicut qui ꜭux rumal ri ma habi xqui chapo.
sentences.l: (Chi) burning(?) again-then their-heart because the not there-was they-caught.
sentences.i: Then their hearts burned (?), because they had caught none of them.
sentences.n: catat 'burning' has plain c (Brasseur gatat); the sense follows his 'dont le cœur aussi brûlait de colère' and is inferred (toggle by the letters). qui ꜭux 'their heart' (MS qux, read ꜭ with Brasseur). ma habi xqui chapo 'there was none they caught'.

sentences.t: Xpe curi hunchic v xambe chic, ca ꜩoꜩotic ta xpetic.
sentences.l: Came then-the one-more its-last(?) now, hopping(?) when it-came.
sentences.i: Then one more came, the very last (?), hopping (?) along as it came.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). hunchic 'one more' (toggle junchik). v xambe 'the last of them' is not otherwise known (Brasseur 'tout le dernier'; inferred). ca ꜩoꜩotic 'hopping, skipping': ca- (ongoing) + a doubled root ꜩoꜩ + -otic, the kind of word that paints a movement (Brasseur 'en sautant'; inferred; toggle by the letters).

sentences.t: Catecut xqui cateh, xqui ze cut pa cul ri cho; catepuch xqui chapo, xqui yoteh puch chirih v vi; xrah qui bio.
sentences.l: Then-then they-blocked(?)-it, they-wrapped(?) then in cloth(?) the rat; then-also they-caught-it, they-squeezed(?) also behind its head; wanted they-choke(?)-it.
sentences.i: Then they headed it off (?) and caught it up in a cloth (?), the rat; and so they seized it and squeezed it (?) at the back of its head, meaning to choke it (?).
sentences.n: cho 'rat': the modern word for rat and mouse is ch'o, and the toggle restores the ch' (the word is certain; Ximénez writes plain ch). xqui cateh 'they blocked it', with plain c as in Brasseur's cateh, after his 'lui barrant le passage' (inferred). xqui ze 'they wrapped it' is not otherwise known (Brasseur 'prirent … dans un mouchoir'; a guess). pa cul 'in a cloth': cul is a doubtful reading (the l could be read t, cut), with plain c where Brasseur has qul; 'cloth' follows him (the modern k'ul is a blanket; toggle by the letters). xqui yoteh 'they squeezed' (Brasseur 'le serrèrent vivement à la tête'; inferred). chirih v vi 'behind its head': chi + r- + ih 'back', and vi 'head' (toggle wi'). xrah qui bio 'they wanted to choke it': bio is not otherwise known (Brasseur 'voulaient l'étouffer'; a guess).

sentences.t: Xqui poroh vhe chuvi ꜫaꜫ; ta xu cam ri vhe cho, ma habi rizmal vhe;
sentences.l: They-burned its-tail on-top fire; then it-took the its-tail rat, not there-was its-hair its-tail;
sentences.i: They burned its tail over the fire, and so the rat came by its tail, a tail with no hair on it;
sentences.n: xqui poroh 'they burned it' (modern poroj 'burn'). chuvi ꜫaꜫ 'over the fire', ꜫaꜫ with two tresillos (Brasseur gag; toggle q'aq'). xu cam ri vhe cho 'the rat took its tail', that is, came to have the tail it has (Brasseur 'c'est alors que le Rat commença à porter la queue'; toggle k'am). rizmal vhe 'the hair of its tail' (r- + izmal 'hair'): why the rat's tail is bare.

sentences.t: are naipu vbac vvach ta xrah biye cumal ꜭaholab ri Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.l: this likewise its-bone its-face when wanted going(?) by-them boys the Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.i: and so too its eyes, which all but popped out (?) at the hands of the boys, Hunahpu and Xbalanque.
sentences.n: naipu 'likewise' (toggle naypu, as in earlier parts). vbac vvach 'its eyes', the house rendering (word for word 'the bone of its face'). xrah biye 'they were about to go out': biye 'going' as in an earlier part (inferred); Brasseur 'comme s'ils eussent été pressés dehors'. Why the rat's eyes bulge. cumal ꜭaholab 'by the boys' (MS q-shaped letter, read ꜭ, as in all earlier parts).

sentences.t: “Ma ta qui camic ivumal; mavi are ipatan ri abixic ꜭo ive,” xꜭha ri cho.
sentences.l: “Not (ta) I(?) dying by-you; not this your-service the field-work there-is to-you,” said the rat.
sentences.i: “Do not let me die at your hands! Clearing a field is not the work that is yours,” said the rat.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). Ma ta … 'let it not be': ma with the optative ta. qui camic is read 'I die' as Brasseur takes it (Ma-ta qu'in camic), but no n is written: qui is read as quin, k- + in 'me', with the n not written (inferred; toggle by the letters). ivumal 'by you (pl.)'. ipatan 'your service, your task'. ꜭo ive 'that is yours': ꜭo 'there is' is written go in the MS and read ꜭ with Brasseur's qo, as everywhere in this part (toggle k'o). The rat tells them field work is not their calling; the ball game is.

sentences.t: “Apa ꜭo vi que chabiyh nacut?” xeꜭha curi ꜭaholab chire cho.
sentences.l: “Where there-is (vi) (que) you-say now-then?” they-said then-the boys to-it rat.
sentences.i: “And where is it, then, this thing you would tell?” said the boys to the rat.
sentences.n: Apa ꜭo vi 'where is it', the question of a thing to be found. que chabiyh 'you tell': ch- + a- 'you (one)' + biyh 'say' (as in earlier parts), with que not clear here (toggle by the letters; Brasseur que ch'a biyh). chabiyh has plain ch where Brasseur prints ch'. nacut 'now then': na + cut (toggle nak'ut).

sentences.t: “La quin iꜩocopih ta na bala; ꜭo nu ꜩih chi nu pam; cate cut chin biyh chive; chi ya ta na zquin vecha,” xꜭha ri cho.
sentences.l: “(La) me you-release (ta) first bala; there-is my-word in my-belly; then then I-shall-say to-you; let-give (ta) first little my-food,” said the rat.
sentences.i: “Let me go for a while, please: there is a word of mine in my belly, and then I will tell it to you. But first give me a little of my food,” said the rat.
sentences.n: La, the particle of a courteous request (as in earlier parts). quin iꜩocopih 'you (pl.) release me': qu- + in 'me' + i- 'you (pl.)' + ꜩocopih, the modern tzoqopij 'let go' (the word certain; toggle tzoqopij, q for the c). ta na 'please, first'. bala unexplained, as in Vꜩ bala. ꜭo nu ꜩih chi nu pam 'there is my word in my belly', the thing he knows. chin biyh 'I shall tell': ch- + in 'I' + biyh. chi ya ta na 'give first'. zquin 'a little' follows Brasseur ('un peu'; inferred; toggle skin). vecha 'my food' (v- + echa).

sentences.t: “Cate chi ca yao avecha; chabiyh na,” xu ꜭhaxic.
sentences.l: “Then (chi) we-give-it your-food; you-say first,” it-was-told.
sentences.i: “Afterwards we will give you your food; tell it first,” he was told.
sentences.n: Cate chi ca yao 'afterwards we shall give': ca 'we' + yao (ya 'give' + -o). avecha 'your food': av-, a- before a vowel. chabiyh na 'tell it first', here a command. xu ꜭhaxic 'he was told', the passive of ꜭha 'say' (as xuꜭhaxic in earlier parts, here written apart).

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala. Are bari rech icahau ri Hunhunahpu, Vucub Hunahpu vbi, ri xe cam chi Xibalba;
sentences.l: “Good bala. This (bari) belonging your-father the Hunhunahpu, Vucub Hunahpu their-name, the they-died at Xibalba;
sentences.i: “Very well. These, then, are the things of your fathers, Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu by name, who died in Xibalba:
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). Vꜩ bala 'Very well', the house rendering. Are bari 'these are': bari is not otherwise known, perhaps ba, a particle of emphasis, + ri (inferred; toggle by the letters). rech 'the belongings of': r- + ech. icahau 'your father' (i- 'your (pl.)' + cahau), singular for the two brothers. Hunhunahpu, Vucub Hunahpu, the twins' father and uncle, who died in Xibalba in the earlier parts.

sentences.t: ꜭo cu canoc ri queꜩabal, xequel canoc chuvi ha: ri qui bate, qui pachcab, qui quic puch.
sentences.l: there-is then left the their-gear-for-play, hanging(?) left on-top house: the their ring, their hand-guard, their rubber also.
sentences.i: their gear for play is still left there, hanging (?) up at the top of the house: their rings, their hand-guards, and their rubber ball.
sentences.n: ꜭo cu canoc 'there is still left'. Brasseur's K'iche' omits ri queꜩabal, xequel canoc and prints only qo cu canoc chuvi ha ri qui bate; the image has the words, and his French renders them ('les instruments de leur divertissement, qui sont demeurés suspendus'). queꜩabal 'their gear for play', as in 009 (toggle ketz'ab'al; inferred). xequel is doubtful: perhaps xe quel 'they hang', the quel of ¶13 and ¶17 (xe quel vi), or xe ꜭel; 'hanging' follows the story and Brasseur's 'demeurés suspendus' (a guess; toggle by the letters). chuvi ha 'on top of the house' (ha 'house', toggle ja). qui bate, qui pachcab, qui quic puch 'their rings, their hand-guards, their rubber ball', the ball player's gear of 009 and 010 (bate and pachcab guesses after Brasseur's 'anneaux', 'gants'; quic, the word for blood and for rubber, here the ball; toggle kik').

sentences.t: Xa mavi ca rah chi vach rumal ivatit, rumal ri are xcam vi icahau.”
sentences.l: Only not one-wants-it at face because-of your-grandmother, because the this he-died (vi) your-father.”
sentences.i: But no one wants them before your eyes, because of your grandmother, because it was for these that your fathers died.”
sentences.n: ca rah 'one wants': c- (ongoing) + r- 'he, she, it' (the ergative: the verb is active, not passive) + ah 'want', with no doer named, and the grandmother as the cause (rumal ivatit 'because of your grandmother'; Brasseur 'on n'a pas voulu … à cause de votre aïeule'). The two rumal make a pair. chi vach 'before (your) face', the prefix not written. ivatit 'your (pl.) grandmother': iv- before a vowel. rumal ri are xcam vi 'because it was for this that he died': vi points back to the cause. xcam, singular 'he died' (toggle xkam, the 'die' verb, not 'take').

sentences.t: “Ma quiꜩih avetaam?” xeꜭha curi ꜭaholab chire cho.
sentences.l: “(Ma) truly you-know?” they-said then-the boys to-it rat.
sentences.i: “Do you truly know this?” said the boys to the rat.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). Ma … ? asks a question. quiꜩih 'truly' (toggle qitzij). avetaam 'you know it': av- 'you (one)' before a vowel + etaam 'know' (modern eta'm). The toggle gives awetaam, the double vowel kept as in the published vetaam (wetaam, 007, 008, 012).

sentences.t: Nim xquicot qui ꜭux ta xqui tao vꜩihel quic.
sentences.l: Greatly rejoiced their-heart when they-heard its-news rubber.
sentences.i: Their hearts rejoiced greatly when they heard the news of the rubber ball.
sentences.n: Nim xquicot qui ꜭux 'their hearts rejoiced greatly': nim 'great', xquicot 'rejoiced' (toggle xkikot). xqui tao 'they heard it' (ta 'hear' + -o). vꜩihel quic 'the news of the ball': ꜩih 'word' + -el, with v- 'its' (toggle utzijel; Brasseur 'l'histoire de la pelote élastique').

sentences.t: Ta xu biyh cho, ta xqui ya cut recha cho.
sentences.l: When it-said rat, then they-gave then its-food rat.
sentences.i: When the rat had told it, they gave the rat its food.
sentences.n: xu biyh 'he told it' (v- 'he'). recha 'its food' (r- + echa), what the rat asked for in ¶9.

sentences.t: “Are curi recha ri: ixim, zaquil ic, quinac, pec, cacou; are cut avech ri; vve naquila cuvvn chi mezcutahinac, avech cut, cha cuxu,” xuꜭhax curi cho cumal Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.l: “This then-the its-food the: maize, white chile, bean, pek, cacao; this then yours the; if anything stored(?) (chi) swept-up(?), yours then; you-gnaw(?),” was-told then-the rat by-them Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.i: “This, then, shall be your food: maize, white chile, beans, pek and cacao; these are yours. And if anything is stored away (?) or swept up (?), that is yours too: you shall gnaw it (?),” the rat was told by Hunahpu and Xbalanque.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). The list of foods: ixim 'maize'; zaquil ic 'white chile' (zaquil 'white', ic 'chile', modern ik, a different word from ic 'moon', ik', so the toggle restores nothing; Brasseur 'le chilé blanc'); quinac 'beans', the modern kinaq', the word certain (Brasseur quinag; toggle kinaq'); pec, a kind of cacao of lesser quality, as Brasseur explains ('sorte de cacao de qualité inférieure'; the modern pek is pataxte), not the pec 'cave' of earlier parts (toggle pek); cacou 'cacao' (toggle by the letters, kakow; the modern word is kakaw). avech 'yours': av- + ech, the ech of rech. vve 'if' (toggle uwe, as in earlier parts). cuvvn: the first vowel is unclear (a or u), Brasseur's quvun taken; with mezcutahinac it follows his 'quelque chose de gardé ou d'oublié', and both senses are guesses: cuvvn 'stored away', mezcutahinac perhaps from mez 'sweep' (+ -inac), 'swept up' (toggle both by the letters). cha cuxu 'you shall gnaw it' (Brasseur 'tu le grignoteras'; inferred). xuꜭhax 'he was told' (toggle xuch'ax).

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala, ix ꜭaholab; naquila cu quin vchah, vve quril ri ivatit?” xꜭha cut.
sentences.l: “Good bala, you boys; anything then I say(?), if she-sees-me(?) the your-grandmother?” it-said then.
sentences.i: “Very well, boys. But what shall I say (?), if your grandmother sees me (?)?” said the rat.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). naquila cu quin vchah 'what then shall I say': naquila 'what, anything'; quin 'I' (k- + in); vchah is not otherwise known, and 'say' follows Brasseur ('quoi donc je dirai'; a guess; toggle by the letters). vve quril ri ivatit is a doubtful division (Brasseur uve qui riri yv atit). quril is taken as qu- (k- + in 'me', the n not written) + r- 'she' + il 'see', 'she sees me', after Brasseur's 'si votre aïeule me voit' (inferred; toggle by the letters).

sentences.t: “Mavi chi ꜩac a ꜭux; oh ꜭolic, coh nohinic ꜭo ru ꜭhaxic ri catit.
sentences.l: “Not let-fall your-heart; we are-here, we-are-ready(?), there-is its-saying the our-grandmother.
sentences.i: “Do not lose heart. We are here, and we are ready (?) with what is to be said to our grandmother.
sentences.n: Mavi chi ꜩac a ꜭux 'let your heart not fall': ꜩac 'fall' (toggle tzaq), a ꜭux 'your heart' (MS gux, read ꜭ with Brasseur's qux). oh ꜭolic 'we are here', as in 015. coh nohinic 'we are ready' follows Brasseur ('nous sommes tout prêts'), perhaps from noh 'fill' (inferred; toggle by the letters). ꜭo ru ꜭhaxic ri catit 'there is what is to be said to our grandmother': ꜭo written go, read ꜭ; ru ꜭhaxic 'its being said', r- + u + ꜭhax + -ic (the u not clear; toggle ru ch'axik). ri catit is the twins' own grandmother in their speech (toggle qatit).

sentences.t: Xa huzu ca ca ya acanoc xiquin ha; ta cu ho co apanoc, huzu cat opon chiri xe quel vi;
sentences.l: Only quickly (ca) we-put up corner house; when then we-go there-is away, quickly you-shall arrive there they-hang(?) (vi);
sentences.i: We will quickly set you up at the corner of the house; and when we have gone off (?), go at once to the place where they hang;
sentences.n: huzu 'quickly' (toggle jusuk, as in earlier parts). ca ca ya acanoc 'we put (you) up': ca 'we' + ya 'give, put' + acanoc 'up' (acan 'climb' + -oc; toggle aq'anoq). The first ca is not clear; it may be cat 'you' with its t not written (a guess; toggle by the letters). xiquin ha 'the corner of the house', word for word 'the ear of the house' (Brasseur 'ce coin de la maison'). ta cu ho co apanoc 'when we go away': ho 'we go' (toggle jo, as in earlier parts); co is written with a plain c, the same word as ꜭo 'there is' (toggle k'o); apanoc 'away' (toggle apanoq). cat opon 'you shall arrive there'. xe quel vi 'where they hang', quel taken as 'hang' (inferred; see ¶10's xequel; toggle by the letters).

sentences.t: chiri cut ca quil vi pu tum ha, xa pa cah ca quil vi,” xeꜭha cut chire cho.
sentences.l: there then is-seen(?) (vi) in-the cords(?) house, only in sky is-seen(?) (vi),” they-said then to-it rat.
sentences.i: there they are to be seen (?), among the cords of the roof (?); only up high are they to be seen (?),” they said to the rat.
sentences.n: ca quil vi 'they are seen there': quil has plain c (Brasseur k'il), taken as ca (ongoing) + qu-, the 'they' of xquil 'they saw' (¶17), + il 'see': 'they see them', that is, they are seen (inferred; Brasseur reads 'que nous voyions'; toggle by the letters), twice, the second line repeating the first. pu tum ha 'in the cords of the house': Brasseur explains tum as any twisted cord or thong used to lash the timbers of a roof (a guess here; the tum of 015 was 'brambles'). xa pa cah 'only in the sky', up under the roof (toggle kaj). Brasseur's text reads xa pu ka ti ca kil vi here, which the image does not have.

sentences.t: Ta xqui pixabah hun acab; xcam qui naoh ri Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.l: Then they-counselled one night; they-took their-thought the Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.i: So they laid their plans for a night (?); Hunahpu and Xbalanque took counsel together.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). xqui pixabah 'they counselled, gave their charge' (toggle pixab'aj, as in earlier parts); with hun acab 'one night' the sense is that the plan was made through the night (inferred; Brasseur 'ayant avisé pour une nuit'). acab, plain c (toggle aq'ab'). xcam qui naoh 'they took counsel', as in ¶1 (toggle xk'am).

sentences.t: Qui cu tiquil quih xe oponic.
sentences.l: (Qui) then planted sun they-arrived-there.
sentences.i: Right at noon (?) they arrived.
sentences.n: tiquil quih 'the planted (standing) sun', noon, as 015's ticoh 'when the sun stands' (Brasseur 'à midi précis'; inferred). quih has a plain qu (Brasseur gih); it is taken as q'ih 'sun, day', the house ꜫih, and the toggle restores the q' (as acab aq'ab'). Qui is not clear (perhaps qui 'truly', as in 015; toggle by the letters).

sentences.t: Ma cu calah ri cho; cu caam ta xe oponic.
sentences.l: Not then visible the rat; it-carries(?) when they-arrived-there.
sentences.i: The rat was not to be seen: they carried it hidden (?) as they arrived.
sentences.n: The one paragraph Ximénez indents in this part begins here. calah 'visible' (toggle q'alaj, as in earlier parts). cu caam 'carried': the cucaam of 012–014 written apart (toggle ku kaam by the letters, as 014); Brasseur 'Portant le Rat sans le montrer'.

sentences.t: Hun ri yacalic xoc pa ha, hun cu xoc xiquin ha; libah chi xu ya acanoc ri cho.
sentences.l: One the upright entered in house, one then entered corner house; instantly (chi) he-put up the rat.
sentences.i: One went straight (?) into the house, and the other went to the corner of the house, and at once he set the rat up there.
sentences.n: Hun … hun 'one … the other'. yacalic 'standing upright' (toggle yakalik), here taken as going in openly (inferred; Brasseur prints yaçalic, 'délibérément'). xiquin ha 'the corner of the house', as in ¶13. libah chi 'at once' (Brasseur libahchi; toggle lib'aj chi). xu ya acanoc 'he put it up', as the twins had planned (¶13).

sentences.t: Ta xqui ꜩonoh cut qui va chire catit: “Xa chi cutu ca ti, ca ca raih ri cutum ic, ix catit,” xeꜭha cut.
sentences.l: Then they-asked then their-food to-her their-grandmother: “Only let-grind(?) our-eating, (ca) we-want the ground(?) chile, you our-grandmother,” they-said then.
sentences.i: Then they asked their grandmother for their meal: “Just grind (?) something for us to eat; we have a craving for chile sauce, grandmother,” they said.
sentences.n: xqui ꜩonoh 'they asked for': the modern tz'onoj 'ask', the word certain; the MS has the plain tz ligature and the toggle supplies the tz' (as 015's tz'iloj). qui va 'their food' (toggle wa). chi cutu 'grind it': cut 'grind, crush' (Brasseur 'broyez'; inferred). ca ti 'our eating' (ti 'eat', as in earlier parts). ca ca raih 'we want': ca (ongoing) + ca 'we' + raih, as raih 'desire' in earlier parts (inferred). cutum ic 'ground chile', chile sauce (Brasseur cutum ic, 'chilmol'); ic is the chile, modern ik, not ic 'moon' (toggle ik).

sentences.t: Catecut xcut qui ti hun lac vvaal, xtiquibax chi qui vach.
sentences.l: Then-then was-ground(?) their-eating one plate its-liquid, was-set at their face.
sentences.i: Then their meal was ground (?): a bowl of broth was set before them.
sentences.n: xcut qui ti 'their meal was ground': x- + cut, here taken as passive in sense (inferred; Brasseur 'on leur prépara'). hun lac vvaal 'a plate of its liquid', broth (lac 'plate', toggle laq; vvaal 'its water', as in earlier parts). xtiquibax 'it was set': tiquiba 'plant, set' (as ¶1) + -x, the passive (toggle xtikib'ax).

sentences.t: Xavi qui michbal re catit, qui chuch puch; xqui ꜩahiꜩah ca ha pa quebal: “Quiꜩih chaquih ca chi; chi cama cu quia,” xeꜭha chire catit.
sentences.l: Just their-means-of-tricking of their-grandmother, their mother also; they-poured-out(?) (ca) water in jar: “Truly dry our-mouth; let-fetch(?) then drink(?),” they-said to-her their-grandmother.
sentences.i: It was only a trick on their grandmother, and on their mother: they poured out (?) the water in the jar. “Truly our mouths are dry; go and fetch us a drink (?),” they said to their grandmother.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). Xavi qui michbal 'it was only their trick': mich, the root of michouic in ¶2, + -bal, the means (inferred). re catit, qui chuch puch 'on their grandmother, and on their mother', the couplet of ¶2. xqui ꜩahiꜩah 'they poured out': a doubled root (perhaps tzaj 'dry, drain'), after Brasseur 'ayant renversé l'eau de la cruche' (inferred; toggle by the letters). ca ha 'the water' (Brasseur cu ha; ca not clear). quebal 'jar' (Brasseur 'cruche'; inferred, the keb'al of 'household things' in an earlier part). chaquih ca chi 'our mouths are dry': chaquih 'dry', chi 'mouth' (toggle chi'). chi cama cu quia 'fetch us a drink' (Brasseur ch'y qama k'uquia, 'allez donc nous chercher à boire'; a guess): cama as 'take, fetch' (the kama of an earlier part), quia not clear. The cu is written heavily over another letter, probably a corrected ca.

sentences.t: “Ve,” xꜭha cut, ta xbec.
sentences.l: “Yes,” she-said then, then she-went.
sentences.i: “Yes,” she said, and off she went.
sentences.n: Ve 'yes' (Brasseur 'Oui'; toggle we). xbec 'she went' (be 'go' + -c).

sentences.t: Are cut que va canoc; ma cu quiꜩih ta que numic, xa qui moyvachibal xqui bano.
sentences.l: This then they eat left; not then truly (ta) they hungry, only their-means-of-blinding-face they-made-it.
sentences.i: As for them, they stayed behind eating; but they were not truly hungry (?): it was only a way of blinding her eyes that they made.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). que va canoc 'they stayed eating': que (ongoing) 'they' + va 'eat', with canoc 'left behind' (toggle kanoq). que numic 'they were hungry': num 'hunger' + -ic (modern numik); Brasseur takes it as thirst ('aucun besoin de boire'), and 'hungry' is the word's own sense (inferred here). qui moyvachibal 'their means of blinding the face': moy 'blind' + vach 'face, eye' + -ibal (toggle moywachib'al), a ruse to keep her from seeing.

sentences.t: Ta xquil cut ri cho chupan cutum ic, colon vloc ri cho chirih quic xe quel vi pu vi ha.
sentences.l: Then they-saw then the rat in chile-sauce; freed(?) hither the rat behind rubber they-hang(?) (vi) at-its top house.
sentences.i: Then they saw the rat in the chile sauce: the rat had got clear (?) up behind the rubber ball, where the things hung at the top of the house.
sentences.n: xquil 'they saw', without the -o (toggle xkil). chupan 'inside it': chi + v- + pan, the MS ending in n (Brasseur chupam); the toggle gives chupam, as for chupan in 011. The twins see the rat in the sauce, as in a mirror (inferred: the rat is up at the roof, and only its reflection can be in the bowl). colon vloc 'freed, come clear' (kol 'save, free'; inferred, as in an earlier part). chirih quic 'behind the ball'. xe quel vi pu vi ha 'where they hang at the top of the house' (quel as in ¶13; pu vi 'at its head', toggle wi').

sentences.t: Ta xquilo pa cutum ic, ta xqui tac cut hun xan, ri chicop ri xan queheri vz; xopon chi a.
sentences.l: When they-saw-it in chile-sauce, then they-sent then one xan, the animal the xan like gnat; it-arrived at river.
sentences.i: When they had seen it in the chile sauce, they sent off a xan, the creature called xan, which is like a gnat; it came to the river.
sentences.n: xquilo 'they saw it', with the -o of a transitive verb. xqui tac 'they sent' (toggle taq). xan is kept as the name of the creature; the text itself says it is like vz 'gnat, mosquito' (modern us; Brasseur 'moucheron'). chi a 'at the river' (a 'river, water', as in earlier parts).

sentences.t: Are cu xvoro vvach quebal atit, xa yacal ha chel chuvach vquebal; chu tiho, xma chi ꜩapitah vi vvach quebal.
sentences.l: This then pierced its-face jar old-woman; only raised water let-go-out on-its-face her-jar; she-tried-it, not (chi) was-closed (vi) its-face jar.
sentences.i: And it pierced the side of the old woman's jar, and the water welled up and ran out through the side of her jar; she tried, but the side of the jar could not be stopped.
sentences.n: xvoro 'it pierced it' (modern wor 'bore, pierce'; toggle xworo). vvach quebal 'the face of the jar', its side. yacal 'raised', welling (inferred). chel 'goes out' has plain ch (Brasseur ch'el; toggle by the letters), the el 'go out' of earlier parts. chu tiho 'she tried' has plain ch (Brasseur ch'u; toggle chu tijo). ꜩapitah 'be closed': the modern tz'apij 'close, stop up', the word certain; the toggle supplies the tz' on the plain ligature (tz'apitaj), as in ¶19.

sentences.t: “Naquipa mi xu ban ri catit? Oh hizabah chi ya, coh vꜩin rumal chaquih chi,” xeꜭha chic chire qui chuch, ta xqui tac vbic.
sentences.l: “What (mi) she-did-it the our-grandmother? We choking(?) for water, we-are-finished(?) because-of dry mouth,” they-said again to-her their mother, then they-sent thither.
sentences.i: “What can our grandmother be doing? We are choking (?) for water; we are done for (?) with our dry mouths,” they said to their mother, and sent her off.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). Naquipa mi xu ban 'what has she done': mi 'just now' with the completive. ri catit is their own grandmother in their speech (toggle qatit). hizabah 'choking' is not otherwise known (Brasseur 'nous étouffons faute d'eau'; a guess; toggle by the letters). chi ya 'for water' (ya 'river, water', as in earlier parts). coh vꜩin 'we are done for': vꜩin 'be complete, finished', as in an earlier part (Brasseur 'nous mourons de soif'; inferred). chaquih chi 'dry mouth' (toggle chi'). xqui tac vbic 'they sent her off' (vbic 'thither').

sentences.t: Catecut xu ca cat vla cho ri quic; xcah vla pu tum ha, ruc bate, pachcab, quum.
sentences.l: Then-then it-(ca)-cut(?) hither rat the rubber; came-down hither from-the cords(?) house, with ring, hand-guard, leather(?).
sentences.i: Then the rat went and cut (?) the rubber ball loose, and down it came from the cords (?) of the roof, with the rings, the hand-guards and the leather (?).
sentences.n: xu ca cat 'it cut it': cat has plain c (Brasseur gat; 'cut', after his 'le Rat alla couper', inferred; toggle by the letters); ca is not clear (perhaps 'go', Brasseur 'alla'). vla 'hither', down toward them (toggle ula). xcah vla 'it came down' (toggle xqaj, as in earlier parts). pu tum ha 'from the cords of the house', as ¶13. ruc 'with', plain c (toggle ruk'). quum is printed as written, with a q-shaped letter with a descender, not the tz ligature: a doubtful reading. Brasseur reads tzuum 'leather', the ꜩuun 'leathers' of 009's list, and 'leather' follows him (a guess; toggle by the letters).

sentences.t: Xqui mahix tah cut; cate xpe que vah pa be vbeel hom.
sentences.l: They-seized(?) (tah) then; then came they hid(?) in road its-road ball-court.
sentences.i: They snatched them up (?), and then went and hid them (?) on the road, the way to the ball court.
sentences.n: xqui mahix 'they seized them' (Brasseur 'Ils s'en emparèrent immédiatement'; inferred, perhaps from mah 'take away'; toggle by the letters), with tah. xpe que vah 'they came and hid them': vah is taken as evah 'hide' with its e written in que (inferred; Brasseur prints qu'euah; toggle by the letters). pa be vbeel hom 'on the road, the road of the ball court': vbeel 'its road' (the image has b, where Brasseur prints u heel); hom 'ball court' (toggle jom).

sentences.t: Catecut xe be chic ruꜭ catit chi ya; ca tahin curi catit, qui chuch, ꜩapi vvach quebal huhun.
sentences.l: Then-then they-went again with-her their-grandmother at river; were-at-it then-the their-grandmother, their mother, closing its-face jar each.
sentences.i: Then they went off to their grandmother at the river; and their grandmother and their mother were at work there, each of them, stopping the side of the jar.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). ruꜭ catit 'to their grandmother', narrative (toggle katit). chi ya 'at the river' (Brasseur ehi ya, OCR). ca tahin 'they were busy': tahin, the progressive (toggle tajin). ꜩapi 'closing', the tz'apij of ¶17 (the tz' supplied; inferred for this short form). huhun 'each one' (toggle jujun).

sentences.t: Catecut ta xe oponic huhun chi cu chi vvb, ta xe oponic chi ya: “Naquipa mi xi bano? Xa mi xcoz ca ꜭux, xoh petic,” xeꜭha.
sentences.l: Then-then when they-arrived-there each (chi) then (chi) blowgun, when they-arrived-there at river: “What (mi) you-did-it? Only (mi) tired our-heart, we-came,” they-said.
sentences.i: Then they arrived, each with his blowgun; they came to the river: “What have you been doing? Our hearts grew weary of waiting, and so we came,” they said.
sentences.n: huhun chi cu chi vvb 'each with his blowgun': chi cu chi is not clear (Brasseur also huhun chi cu chi uub; 'with' after his 'avec leur sarbacane'). vvb 'blowgun' (toggle wub', as in earlier parts). xi bano 'you (pl.) have done': x- + i- 'you (pl.)' + bano. xcoz ca ꜭux 'our hearts grew tired': coz 'tired' (modern kos), ca ꜭux 'our heart' (MS gux, read ꜭ with Brasseur's qux). 'of waiting' is the English's; Brasseur supplies the same.

sentences.t: “Chivila na vvach nu quebal, mavi ca ꜩapitahic,” xꜭha catit.
sentences.l: “You-look-at-it first its-face my-jar, not it-is-closed,” said their-grandmother.
sentences.i: “Look at the side of my jar: it cannot be stopped,” said their grandmother.
sentences.n: Chivila 'look at it (pl.)': ch- + iv- 'you (pl.)' + il 'see' + -a (toggle chiwila). nu quebal 'my jar'. ca ꜩapitahic 'it is closed' (toggle tz'apitajik, the tz' supplied as in ¶17).

sentences.t: Libah chicut xqui ꜩapih chic; hunam cut xe pe chic, e nabe chuvach catit.
sentences.l: Instantly again-then they-closed-it again; together then they-came again, they first before their-grandmother.
sentences.i: At once they stopped it, and they came back together, going on ahead of their grandmother.
sentences.n: Libah 'at once' (toggle lib'aj). xqui ꜩapih 'they closed it' (toggle tz'apij, the tz' supplied). hunam 'alike, together' (toggle junam). e nabe chuvach catit 'they first, before their grandmother': the twins walk ahead.

sentences.t: Quehecut v canaic quic ri.
sentences.l: Thus-then its-being-left rubber the.
sentences.i: And so the rubber ball was left to them (?).
sentences.n: Quehecut 'thus then' (toggle Keje'k'ut). v canaic 'its being left': canah 'remain' + -ic, with the h not written (inferred; Brasseur 'comment leur fut livrée la pelote'). The episode of the ball gear ends here; the next part begins with the twins going to play ball (MS Que quicot chicut xebec).
